content:
The age of the universe is estimated to be approximately **13.8 billion years**.

This measurement is based on data collected by the Planck space observatory, which analyzed the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB)—the leftover radiation from the Big Bang. By studying the patterns in this light, scientists have been able to calculate the rate at which the universe is expanding and, by tracing that expansion backward, determine its age.

**A note on current scientific debate:**
While 13.8 billion years is the standard, widely accepted figure, there is currently an active and exciting debate in the scientific community known as the "Hubble Tension." 

Some measurements of the expansion rate of the universe (using nearby stars and supernovae) suggest that the universe might be slightly younger, while others (using the CMB) suggest it is slightly older. Cosmologists are currently working to resolve this discrepancy, but 13.8 billion years remains the most precise estimate we have today.
